result.summary: The page is largely well-designed, but there is one clear data/formatting bug: the 'Smash Bros Burgers' card shows '€NaN delivery' instead of a valid price, indicating a failed numeric parse or missing data. Other observations are minor (horizontally clipped cards at the right edge are likely intentional carousel behavior).

issues.description: The 'Smash Bros Burgers' restaurant card displays '€NaN delivery' as its delivery fee. 'NaN' (Not a Number) is a raw programming error value leaking into the UI, which looks broken and unprofessional and confuses users about the actual delivery cost.
issues.suggestion: Fix the data pipeline or formatting logic so the delivery fee always resolves to a valid number or a proper fallback (e.g. 'Free delivery' or '€0.00 delivery'). Add a guard that renders a sensible default when the fee value is null/undefined/unparseable instead of interpolating NaN into the string.

issues.description: In the 'Fastest near you' row, the third card ('Trattoria Piccol...') and its title are clipped at the right screen edge. While this may be an intentional horizontal-scroll carousel affordance, there is no visible scroll indicator or peek padding cue beyond the cut-off card.
issues.suggestion: Add a subtle scroll affordance (e.g. partial card peek with consistent edge padding, scroll dots, or a gradient fade) so users clearly understand the row is horizontally scrollable.

issues.description: The favorite/heart buttons on the 'Popular right now' cards rely on an icon-only control with no visible text label, which can be ambiguous for screen-reader and assistive-technology users.
issues.suggestion: Provide accessible labels (e.g. aria-label='Add Tokumaru Ramen Bar to favorites') and ensure the heart icon has sufficient contrast against the dark image background.
